content: Fernwood Systems is a 40-person infrastructure company based in Halifax, Nova Scotia.
In January 2026, Fernwood Systems replaced its timestamp-based build cache with a content-addressed one.
The old cache keyed each artifact on the modification time of the files that produced it.
The new cache keys every artifact on the SHA-256 hash of its declared inputs.
Two builds with identical inputs are guaranteed to resolve to the same cache entry regardless of when they ran.
Median CI build time on Fernwood Systems' main branch fell from 14 minutes to 3 minutes 20 seconds after the migration.
The cache hit rate on Fernwood Systems' main branch now sits at 82 percent, measured over the eight weeks since the cutover.
The migration took six weeks of one engineer's time.
The migration required rewriting 41 build files to declare their inputs explicitly.
Roughly a third of the 41 rewritten build files were reading configuration from the environment without declaring it.
Storage costs rose from $310 to $1,900 per month because of the migration.
The migration caused storage costs to rise because Fernwood Systems retains evicted cache entries for 30 days.
The hardest part of the migration was not the hashing, but teaching the build to be honest about its inputs.
Fernwood Systems evaluated moving to a remote execution cluster at the same time and decided against it for now.
Fernwood Systems expects to revisit the decision to move to a remote execution cluster once the cache hit rate stops improving.
The rollout of the content-addressed cache to the other three engineering teams is planned for the third quarter of 2026.

content: Halcyon Grid Cooperative is a member-owned community-solar cooperative in Duluth, Minnesota with 1,240 subscribing households.
Halcyon Grid Cooperative operates three arrays totalling 8.4 megawatts of nameplate capacity.

Revenue for 2025 was $1.62 million against operating costs of $940,000, giving the cooperative its first operating surplus: $680,000.
